newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Antimony prices should go back up - Chinese official.
newsitem.headline: Antimony prices should go back up - Chinese official.

text.p: Antimony prices have almost hit rock bottom and should start going up again in April, a senior Chinese official said on Tuesday.

Current world prices, at around US$2,200 per tonne, cannot sustain Chinese production and have forced many factories to either lower production or close down, Zheng Feng Ren, director of Hsikwangshan Mining Administration's marketing department, told a conference.
"The price is too low," Zheng said, adding that China has drawn down much of its stockpile.
China is offering US$2,300 per tonne in the international market compared to its offer price of US$2,400 to US$2,500 per tonne in January.
Zheng also said his factories were being forced to increase production of other products such as zinc ingots and would lower antimony production this year.
In 1996, Zheng's mines produced 17,000 tonnes of antimony, but the amount is projected to fall by 10 to 20 percent in 1997.
Zheng also said Chinese mines could only move into the red with antimony prices between US$2,800 and US$3,000 per tonne.
"We hope the price will reach a suitable level and the market will be stable since too many changes are not good for production," he said.
When antimony prices were at a high of US$6,000 per tonne in 1994 and 1995, production in China jumped, leading to increased supplies which then led to a gradual price drop.
